name: Helipterum Rosum
latin: Rhodanthe chlorocephala subsp. rosea (syn. Helipterum roseum, Acroclinium roseum)
grown_as: An everlasting or paper daisy, a half-hardy annual from Western Australia grown for cutting and drying. William's library lists a 'Giant flower mix' in pinks, rose and white. Drawn in pink. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A slender upright annual 30 to 60 cm high, little-branched, the stems thin and wiry.

leaf.outline: Narrow, linear to narrow lance-shaped, 2 to 6 cm long

flower.form: A stiff, papery daisy that stays the same when dried
flower.petals: Not rays: many rows of stiff, shiny, papery, pointed bracts that crackle to the touch
flower.colour: Pink or white (the mix also gives rose)
flower.centre: A yellow disc of tiny tubular florets, sometimes ringed by a narrow dark band of short inner bracts
flower.behind: Overlapping rows of papery bracts, the outer ones small, brownish or silvery
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of slender stems; the bud nods, then the open head faces up. Closes in dull weather

fruit: A fluffy white seed head. Each seed is small and woolly with a ring of feathery white bristles.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are narrow and grey-green.

leaf: narrow linear leaf, smooth-edged and stalkless
bloom: many rows of stiff pointed papery bracts, not soft petals
yellow centre, perhaps with a narrow dark ring
seed: small woolly seed with feathery white bristles
flower: slender stems each topped by one papery pink or white daisy
some buds nodding before they open

look_alikes: Strawflower (Xerochrysum) is bigger and bushier with broader leaves and yellow, orange or red heads. Rhodanthe manglesii has broad, blue-green, stem-clasping leaves and nodding heads. Winged everlasting (Ammobium) is white with winged stems.
